articles.title: Fifa reportedly allowed DR Congo into World Cup despite ineligible player in qualifying
articles.summary: Nigeria filed complaint over ineligible players in playoff. Fifa investigators aware of situation before tournament. Fifa allowed the Democratic Republic of the Congo to compete at this summer’s World Cup despite reports suggesting an internal investigation found that the country had fielded an…
body: The player in question, the goalkeeper Lionel Mpasi, starred for his nation at the tournament, including against England in the last 32. Mpasi, who was born in France and played for Les Bleus at youth level, had never completed the process of switching nationalities, Fifa reportedly found. No punishment was levied against the Congolese federation, Fecofa.

The news will again raise questions over the Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, with a series of governance scandals having brought heightened scrutiny on his position. Fifa’s investigative teams are independent and the president has no input into their proceedings. Fifa is understood to have denied that Infantino played a part in the decision-making process over Mpasi, but his name is likely to remain in focus owing to a former university associate, Véron Mosengo-Omba, being elected unopposed as president of Fecofa this May.

The Nigerian Football Federation submitted a complaint over the DRC apparently fielding ineligible players during a World Cup playoff tie between the nations, which the DRC won on penalties, in November.

articles.title: Portuguese authorities took 83 days to tell Rui Pinto his witness protection was ending
articles.summary: Commission concluded in July threat level was low. Manchester City whistleblower given 10 days’ notice. Portuguese authorities kept Rui Pinto in the dark for almost three months about their decision to end his status as a protected witness and notified the Manchester City whistleblower 10 days…
body: According to documents seen by the Guardian, the special security programmes commission (CPES), which oversees Portugal’s witness protection programme, met on 8 and 9 July to discuss Pinto’s case. It concluded that the threat level against him was low and that the special protection measures were no longer warranted.

Yet it was not until 30 September that Pinto, who has been a protected witness since 2020 after agreeing to grant Portuguese authorities access to millions of files gathered before his arrest, was informed of the decision – 83 days after it had been made.

With 10 days’ notice, Pinto was left with little time to address a number of immediate issues. He needs to find somewhere safe to live and establish a way of supporting himself in a new location, while avoiding contact with family members.

The Guardian contacted the CPES on two occasions seeking details of the criteria and evidence used to determine that Pinto’s protection should be withdrawn. On Wednesday, the commission was also asked to explain the 83-day gap between its decision and the notification. None of the inquiries received a response.

articles.title: 'Bring the magic' - Scotland's Ross eyes World Cup dream
articles.summary: Scotland assistant coach Leanne Ross never played at a World Cup but thinks the current squad has what it takes to get through the play-offs for Brazil 2027.
body: Leanne Ross is Scotland's most decorated player, earning 133 international caps across a career which garnered 14 league titles and 13 major cup medals, but still the national team's assistant coach wants more.
Having reached the 2017 European Championship, Ross was part of the first women's squad to compete at a major tournament, but one thing has eluded her. A World Cup.
Ross retired after the Euros, meaning she did not take part in the 2019 edition in France, but her dream has not been dashed.
Scotland are a wee bit away from booking flights and hotels for Brazil 2027. Up next is a round one play-off double-header against Czech Republic, live on the BBC, but the excitement is building.

articles.title: Manchester City’s glory cannot be taken away from the players, says Kyle Walker
articles.summary: Former captain admits guilty verdict ‘doesn’t look great’ But he insists memories of ‘many trophies’ will remain. Manchester City’s glory years cannot be taken away from the players, despite the club being found guilty of all charges of breaching Premier League financial rules over a nine-year…
body: City have appealed against last week’s seismic judgment of an independent commission that they broke rules between 2009-10 and 2017-18, with the club found to have boosted their income by a staggering amount of more than £900m. Walker spent eight years at City from 2017 to 2025, winning the Champions League as well as 12 major domestic honours. “Obviously it doesn’t look great,” said the current Burnley captain on TalkSport. “It’s in an appeal stage so for me to start commenting on the legal action … it’s not going to do myself justice or anyone involved in it.

“But, at a personal level, I can say the lads, we spent many and many a great year celebrating many trophies and everything like that and that’s something that, whatever happens, they can’t take away from us because we’ve experienced them nights. So, whatever will be, will be, and it’s just down to the appeal now and what goes from there.”

articles.title: Pidcock ‘mad’ after two teammates collide with police motorcyclist in Italy
articles.summary: Pinarello-Q36.5’s Camprubi and Gloag floored in crash. ‘Things like this shouldn’t happen,’ says British rider. Tom Pidcock has admitted he almost quit the Tre Valli Varesine in a rage after a police motorcyclist drove into the peloton and struck two of his Pinarello Q36.5 teammates.
body: Speaking after the race, in which he finished second, Pidcock said: “A police motorbike was going the wrong way down the course and crashed into two of our guys. I wanted to stop racing myself. I was mad. The guys all riding in front of me – for me – and two of them on the floor.”
The British rider’s teammate, Thomas Gloag, was forced to abandon the race while Marcel Camprubi, of Spain, was able to continue, but finished last.
“Luckily Marcel was OK, he could continue,” Pidcock said. “Tom was also OK, in the end, but he stopped the race, and he has some stitches in the knee.”
Camprubi posted images of his smashed bike on social media, with the caption: “Sad that you have to risk your life to race, one month after a tragic accident.”

articles.title: Russell to start from back of Singapore grid after penalty
articles.summary: Britain's George Russell will start from the back of the grid in Sunday's Singapore Grand Prix because of a power-unit penalty from last weekend's race.
body: The Mercedes driver has received a power-unit penalty from a dramatic Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia last Sunday.
The 28-year-old qualified in eighth but was heading for a podium finish before an engine failure forced him to retire from third place with five laps remaining.

Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff has confirmed that Russell needs to take a new power unit this weekend, putting him over the limit on several components and meaning he will be penalised in Singapore.

Russell's retirement last Sunday meant Kimi Antonelli, who finished second behind Max Verstappen, took a big leap towards his first Formula 1 world title as the Italian is now 84 points ahead of his Mercedes team-mate.

articles.title: 'Nothing can take my attention' - Ward on World Cup
articles.summary: Republic of Ireland manager Carla Ward says that "nothing is tempting" her away from her job as they prepare for a World Cup qualifying double-header against Kazakhstan.
body: Republic of Ireland manager Carla Ward says that her focus is on reaching the Women's World Cup amid speculation linking her to a move back to the Women's Super League.
The Republic have a chance to book a spot at next summer's finals in Brazil when they face a play-off against Kazakhstan before, if they progress, a two-legged final against either Belgium or Poland.

Ward, who replaced Eileen Gleeson in January 2025, has been linked with the vacant post at her former club Aston Villa. However, she insists leading the Republic of Ireland to the World Cup is her primary ambition.
"Nothing is tempting when I'm in this job, you know I love this job and I love working here," Ward said.

body: A first Ferrari grand prix victory for Hamilton in Barcelona in June provided hope that he could launch a 2026 title challenge, but an underwhelming run after the summer break saw his deficit to Mercedes' championship leader Kimi Antonelli grow beyond 100 points.

Hamilton ended a streak of six races without a podium by finishing third at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on Sunday, with only a poor choice of starting tyre costing him the chance to use his impressive pace to battle Red Bull's Max Verstappen for victory.
Following that encouraging display, he explained why he has confidence in his team going into next year.

Hamilton told Sky Sports F1: "I think fundamentally we've got a great car, and that's down to an amazing group of people back at the factory, who are really intelligent and have made the right decisions.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson Injury Update: Ravens QB’s Week 5 Status Revealed
articles.summary: Lamar Jackson suffered an ankle injury in Week 4, and the two-time NFL MVP left the game in a walking boot. This is obviously worrisome news for Ravens fans across the globe, but it does not appear to be a serious issue.
body: Since 2019, Lamar Jackson has made it to four Pro Bowls, won two MVP’s, and earned First-Team All-Pro honors three times while consistently guiding Baltimore to winning seasons. While injuries have been an issue throughout his career, he’s still unstoppable when on the field. So far this season, the quarterback has completed 70.8% of his passes for 967 yards, six touchdowns, and just one interception, but he probably won’t add to those numbers this week. According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, Lamar Jackson has a sprained ankle that only gives him “an outside chance” to play against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 5.

Needless to say, this is not ideal for Lamar Jackson and the Ravens, but it could have been worse. Baltimore has one of the league’s most talented rosters, but no team can compete without an elite quarterback under center. It’s worth noting the Ravens haven’t officially ruled him out for Week 5, but even if he misses one or two weeks, it sounds like this is a relatively minor issue.

articles.title: Inter Nationals: 7 goals, 2 assists and 2,342 minutes for the Nerazzurri
articles.summary: The first international window of the 2026/27 season has come to an end after three weeks of action, with Inter players featuring across the UEFA Nations League, international friendlies and Africa Cu...
body: Ange-Yoan Bonny featured twice for Côte d’Ivoire during the international window, with the Elephants involved in Africa Cup of Nations qualifying. The Nerazzurri forward started the opening group match, playing 72 minutes in a 2-0 win over Ghana, before remaining on the bench for the 2-0 away victory against Somalia. Bonny then came on at the start of the second half in Côte d’Ivoire’s final fixture, a 1-0 friendly defeat to Cameroon. After two qualifying matches, Côte d’Ivoire sit joint-top of Group C with Gambia on six points, while Ghana and Somalia remain without a point.

Petar Sucic featured in all four of Croatia’s Nations League matches, starting three of them as Bilic deployed the Nerazzurri midfielder in an attacking midfield role. He played against Czechia, England and twice against Spain, with Croatia recording one win and three defeats across the four fixtures. Sucic totalled 238 minutes during the international window. Croatia sit third in Nations League A Group 3 on three points, behind Spain on 12 and England on nine, with Czechia bottom on zero.

articles.title: 'No excuses' for Reed after injury as he looks to increase Race to Dubai lead
articles.summary: Race to Dubai leader Patrick Reed says becoming the second American to be crowned European No 1 would mean "a lot" and insists he has "no excuses" as he looks to extend his advantage over Rory McIlroy after returning from a shoulder injury.
body: Reed will tee it up at the Open de Espana from Thursday in his first appearance since withdrawing during the second round of the flagship BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth last month.
The 36-year-old - aiming to follow in the footsteps of compatriot Collin Morikawa, who won the Race to Dubai in 2021 - is around 300 points clear of McIlroy with five DP World Tour events remaining.
McIlroy is not playing in Spain this week but is set to appear at the DP World India Championship in New Delhi from October 15.

Reed has topped the standings since February after victories at the Hero Dubai Desert Classic and Qatar Masters sandwiched a play-off defeat at the Bahrain Championship, with the 2018 Masters champion also recording three further top-10 finishes.

articles.title: Kane sums up England legacy on special night - but can he make final step?
articles.summary: Some things are inevitable in life. Harry Kane delivering for England is always one of those inevitabilities. On his momentous, milestone match, he stuck to the script perfectly.
body: On his 125th cap, Kane did what Kane does best under the Wembley arch - stealing the show, leading the way, winning the game for England.
Everyone knew he would score in this match. It's the same feeling you get in every match. But he still gets the buzz.
"I think this is even beyond my wildest dreams," he said after the game. "To be now at 125, it's just an extreme privilege."
This match - and the three goals he contributed to England's cause on his special night - was a perfect summary of Harry Kane's England career.
